findings.impact: A future caller may pass the declared admission function with unpaired inputs, invalidating the intended paired accuracy comparison. No actual dataset mismatch is asserted; the paired protocol remains pending.
findings.problem: The live context is checked, but its bound paired protocol is checked only for the native and bank manifest hashes. Paired role, features, native graph and validation identities may be absent or inconsistent and still pass.
findings.recommendation: Require a defined paired-protocol schema and fixed block; compare its role/features/native-graph/validation identities with the live context, using a separately bound bank input/freeze record for the bank side.
findings.reproduction: source_review_checks.py::check_paired_protocol_gate uses stdlib synthetic role/bundle and a patched feature-identity function. Both conflicting paired identity fields and an identity-free two-manifest-hash document are accepted.
findings.title: Verify paired input identities before admitting the reference

findings.impact: The live-RNG and exact next-update/full-state claim is unsupported for an admitted MPS execution. This is a source branch gap, not a numerical claim that MPS execution was attempted or otherwise supported.

findings.problem: The device resolver accepts arbitrary device types including MPS, while RNG capture/restore stores only CPU Torch and the selected CUDA stream alongside Python/NumPy. MPS stochastic state is omitted.
findings.recommendation: Preserve byte-identical bank reuse by restricting device types in the new native entry to CPU and selected-device CUDA until other-device RNG state and numerical qualification exist; state the limitation in the package.
